 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Christian Cairo's time as a Los Angeles Dodger was brief and unmemorable.
 Claimed off waivers from the New York Mets on Nov. 9, Cairo was designated for assignment Tuesday, Nov. 19, when the Dodgers added several Rule 5-eligible prospects to their 40-man roster.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Two days later, without playing a game in Los Angeles, the Dodgers lost Cairo on waivers to the Toronto Blue Jays .
 MORE: Dodgers pitcher to miss all of 2027 after major elbow surgery 
 In a corresponding roster move, the Jays designated right-handed pitcher Chase Lee for assignment.
 The timing is notable. A lockout is expected to interrupt the sport on Dec. 1, when the Collective Bargaining Agreement between MLB and the MLB Players Association expires. If that happens, teams will not be able to contact (or negotiate with) 40-man roster players until the lockout ends.
 So far, the two sides haven't made progress on resolving the key separator in their bargaining positions: a salary cap. The end of the month is effectively serving as a deadline to acquire major league players across MLB .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Had he cleared waivers, Cairo could have signed a minor league contract in December. Now he's stuck on the fringes of another team's 40-man roster, with the potential of being unable to report to spring training on time in 2027.
 MORE: Dodgers lose former closer to Braves on $35 million contract 
 Cairo posted a .381 OBP at Triple-A in 2026, the highlight of an otherwise middling offensive profile. A fourth-round draft pick out of high school by the Cleveland Guardians in 2019, Cairo has yet to make his major league debut.
 The Blue Jays are Cairo's fourth team in less than three months. He spent the majority of the 2026 season with the Philadelphia Phillies ' top farm team until he was designated for assignment on Sept. 13 and claimed by the Mets two days later.
